title: Choose the visual world for the Network+ pilot
question: The roll assigned the Field Guide. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Field Guide
options.lineage: naturalist field guides: identification plates, field marks, thumb-index tabs, identification keys
options.thesis: Learn a network the way a birder learns birds: spot the field marks, name the thing, key out the fault.
materials: printed plate on cool white paper
colour thumb-index tabs, one per OSI layer
options.viewport: Lesson step: a top bar with ticket number and step count, the Hairline figure as a plate with numbered field-mark callouts, a two-line account below, a predict question as plain choice buttons, and a sticky Back/Next bar.
options.risk: Seven layer colours can turn into confetti if they leak beyond tabs, highlights and data.

raised.raise: One control remaps the whole field live: the subnet mask slider recolours all 256 addresses continuously.
The construction grid is a real state: 'Show addresses' reveals the grid under any figure.
Every device and protocol is a finite cast member with fixed furniture: a species account with name, layer, port and one-line habit.
Practice and summary screens use hairline-ruled modules with small tabbed headers instead of floating cards.

options.label: Assembly Sheet
options.lineage: flat-pack assembly instructions and exploded technical drawings
options.thesis: Each lesson is an instruction sheet: numbered frames, isometric line art, almost no words.
options.viewport: Lesson step: a huge step numeral, the figure in a framed panel, one line of text, and an arrow to the next frame.
options.risk: It's the most literal reading of Hairline itself, so it's the familiar choice and the app could feel like a manual.

options.label: Midnight Transit Map
options.lineage: metro diagrams in enamel: lines, stations, interchanges
options.thesis: The network is a transit system: packets ride lines, routers are interchanges, the module is one line with four stations.
options.viewport: Lesson step on midnight blue: the figure on a dark plate, the packet's route drawn as a coloured line with station ticks per hop, and the step text in a white panel.
options.case: Strongest audience recognition (everyone reads transit maps) and perfect for packet journeys, but weaker for ports and subnetting, which aren't routes.
options.risk: Dark ground plus bright lines drifts toward the neon-on-black look when the colours are not disciplined.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.thesis: Every help-desk ticket is a segmented pass, and the week is a board whose changed rows stay lit until you notice.
materials: one alert amber reserved for change
options.viewport: Lesson step: a pass-style ticket strip on top (ticket no., location, device, objective), the figure below, and status changes flashing amber and holding.
options.case: Tickets map perfectly onto passes and the module home onto a board, but the world adds little inside the teaching figures.
options.risk: Can read as a travel app when the ticket strip dominates the lesson.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.thesis: One slider morphs the whole page live.
options.viewport: A giant glyph with an axis slider.
options.case: Career changers don't identify with type specimens, and the form only fits subnetting.
options.kept: One control remapping the whole field live, kept for the subnet mask slider.
options.risk: Becomes a type demo, not a lesson.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.case: Poster logic, not a learning screen; low audience recognition.
options.kept: The grid as a real, toggleable state.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: A ranked cast of mascots with name plates.
options.case: Exactly the childish tone adult exam-takers reject.
options.kept: A finite cast with fixed furniture, kept as species accounts for each device and protocol.

options.label: Japanese High-Density Web
options.thesis: Pack every pixel with ruled modules.
options.case: Too dense for one-handed phone study in short sessions.
options.kept: Hairline-ruled modules with tabbed headers instead of floating cards.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern learning app in the Brilliant mould, executed with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Progress bar on top, the figure in a rounded card, text below, and a big primary button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other learning app by design.
